experiments.name: dependent vector chain with reset helper
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 100000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'li.w $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr0, $r4; li.w $r5, 1; li.w $r6, 1065353216' --asm 'xvfsqrt.s $xr0, $xr0; xvpickve2gr.w $r4, $xr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr0, $r4'
experiments.notes: vpickve2gr extracts element 0, and/or forces it back to the test value, vreplgr2vr replicates it; the vadd.b baseline is subtracted.

experiments.name: vadd.b reset-helper baseline
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 100000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'li.w $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr0, $r4; li.w $r5, 1; li.w $r6, 1065353216' --asm 'xvadd.b $xr0, $xr0, $xr0; xvpickve2gr.w $r4, $xr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr0, $r4'
experiments.notes: Same helper chain with vadd.b replacing the variable-latency operation.

latencies.notes: Data-dependent. 11 cycles when the input is zero, Inf or NaN; 15 when the result is exact (the input is an even power of two such as 1.0, 4.0 or 0.25); 11 for an exact result from a subnormal input; 39 when the square root needs the full 23-bit mantissa (sqrt(2.0), sqrt(max)); 37 for that case with a subnormal input (sqrt(maxsub)). The long path retires one mantissa bit per cycle (15 + 2*ceil(23/4) = 36), so a square root costs twice the digit time of a divide.

notes: LASX variable-latency floating-point instruction. Latency measured with a reset helper that keeps element 0 at the test value; throughput measured with 8 independent lanes. Ranges cover special values, exact/non-exact cases, subnormals, and overflow/underflow boundaries.
